beyond_gauge: The help line at `scripts/dispatch.sh:164` says the env var keeps user settings, but the condition at line 1476 ignores it for role-resolved seats. An operator who sets it on a `--role` dispatch sees no effect and the help text does not say why.

The dry-run display change at lines 1548-1554 is outside the brief's named scope. It fixed a stale slice that dropped `-p` from the claude dry-run output after the prompt moved to stdin, which criterion 1(a) needed. The preview now prints after `-p`, so the dry-run reads as a positional prompt while the real run at line 1981 feeds stdin. Cosmetic only.
All 10 parser tests were skipped because gawk is absent. Criterion 2 for that suite rests on exit 0 plus the commit stat showing the file untouched, not on the tests executing.

Excluding user scope drops all of the operator's user settings file, including any api key helper or env block such as a proxy base URL. A seat whose auth or routing lives there fails at runtime, which the dry-run tests cannot see. The brief's own measurement shows it works on this machine.

**Test (a) does not guard the stdin fix.** Its fence body is wrapped in `set +e` and `set -e`. I piped that exact body into `bash -e -o pipefail` the way the old code did. The `read` swallowed the trailing `set -e` line, "after" still printed, and the exit was 0. The test fails on the old code only because the old receipt detail omitted stdout. Reverting stdin to the script body while keeping the stdout-in-detail change would leave the test green. Asserting that `line` is empty would close this.

**Criterion 1(a) conflicts with constraint 1.** The literal fence `read -r line; echo "after"` exits 1 under `bash -e` with stdin at end-of-file, because `read` returns 1 and errexit aborts before the echo. I reproduced that. The `set +e` wrapper is the only way to satisfy both, which is what produced the weak test above. This is a brief-level inconsistency, not an implementation error.

**Mixed line endings are rewritten.** The decoder chooses CRLF if any CRLF byte pair exists and re-emits every line with it, and lone CR is normalised the same way. A mixed-ending file therefore has untouched lines changed on disk. The brief only specified pure CRLF and pure LF files.

**Timeout cleanup can still block.** After the group is killed, the last call to `communicate` has no timeout. A fence child that escaped the process group with `setsid` while holding the stdout pipe would hang the apply. The previous code had the same exposure, so this is not a regression.

**Passing verify details now carry stdout.** The receipt keys are unchanged, but the detail value for a passing verify gained the last 20 stdout lines. Anything diffing receipt details across versions will see this.
